Listen to this article Share A new invite-only community for globally minded professionals working in and on Nigeria launched in Lagos recently with a gathering that mixed diplomats, bankers, founders and creatives in one room. Advertisement Advertisement Off Record NG, founded by Opeyemi Oriniowo and Laura Mensah, held its epoch gathering at Atrium by SORA Lagos. The event drew professionals across diplomacy, business, finance, development, technology and the creative industries. The premise is simple: people, not titles. “Off Record is an invite-only, trust-based community for globally minded professionals whose work shapes Nigeria, and whose lives are larger than their titles,” Oriniowo said in his opening speech. “We’re not creating another room where everybody arrives wondering who they need to meet.” “We’re trying to create a room where people arrive curious about who they might discover.” Advertisement Oriniowo said the idea grew from years of moving across diplomacy, business, development, finance and government and noticing how often professionals meet the title first. “We have plenty of places to network,” he said. “What we have fewer of are places to connect. Networking often begins with: ‘What do you do?’ Connection begins with: ‘Who are you?’” he explained. Advertisement The evening put that to test. Guests were assigned colours representing different professional worlds — diplomacy, finance, tech, energy, media and others — then told not to spend the night in their colour. “Find someone from another world,” Oriniowo said. “Resist the temptation to begin with: ‘So, what do you do?’ Ask where they’ve lived. What they’re curious about. What Lagos has taught them. Or simply ask: ‘Who are you when you’re Off Duty?’” Advertisement Advertisement A panel moderated by Arese Ugwu, managing director and CEO of NASD Plc and author of The Smart Money Woman, explored how relationships beyond familiar circles shape careers, belonging and collaboration. Panellists were Jette Bjerrum, Denmark’s consul general in Lagos; Thessa Bagu, founder and managing director of Commercium Africa; and Temitope Runsewe, managing director of Sage Grey Finance Ltd. Launch partners included Pernod Ricard, Sage Grey Finance, KLM, SRS Collection, SORA Lagos, Padel X and Oriflame. Off Record NG will operate as an invite-only community built around trust, shared experiences and mutual growth, the founders said. There is no open membership drive. Growth will come from introductions and relationships built at gatherings. “We spend an extraordinary amount of our lives building careers, companies, institutions and reputations,” Oriniowo said. “But ultimately, so much of the quality of our lives — and often the quality of our work — is determined by something much simpler: the quality of our relationships.” Josephine Okojie-Okeiyi Josephine Okojie-Okeiyi is a journalist with over five years’ reporting experience. She writes on industry, agriculture, commodities, climate change, and environmental issues. She is fellow of Thomson Reuters Foundation and Bloomberg Media Initiative for Africa.
